entries.why_accurate_as_written: This is a STRUCTURAL self-check requirement — it asserts only that a NAMED FIELD (OUTSTANDING_CERTIFICATION_NOT_SATISFIED_BY_THIS_RECORD) exists in the document and is non-empty. It does not itself assert anything about WHETHER the certification occurred; it asserts only that the FIELD carrying that discussion is present. Under either fact pattern — the pre-amendment belief that the recertification had not occurred, or the corrected fact that it had — the field IS present in the append-only parent record (it is never removed, only superseded in substance by OSC-1's replacement text in 2ff84822) and IS non-empty (it carries 666 characters of text, confirmed by direct measurement of the live parent blob). The self-check therefore remains MECHANICALLY TRUE under both fact patterns and needs no supersession.
entries.why_it_was_missed_by_both_prior_sweeps: It matches the swept vocabulary ('outstanding' as a substring of a FIELD NAME being referenced, not as a fresh prose assertion) in a way a naive text sweep would find but a sweep implicitly scoped to 'prose sentences describing the recertification's status' would pass over, because it reads as a structural checklist item rather than a claim. This is the same class of miss this repository's own history has recorded before, under a different name, for a vocabulary sweep that missed a structural alias rather than a fresh restatement — the lesson generalizes: a sweep for describing-vocabulary can both under- and over-catch depending on whether a hit is a fresh assertion or a structural reference to a field's own name, and each hit must be individually classified rather than counted.
